newsitem.title: UK: Three-D ultrasound lets you watch baby yawn.
newsitem.headline: Three-D ultrasound lets you watch baby yawn.

text.p: A new, three-dimensional system for taking ultrasound images of a baby in the womb allows doctors and parents to see a clear view of the foetus moving about and even yawning, Japanese doctors reported on Friday.

Most ultrasound images are fuzzy and unclear and it takes a trained technician to read them. But Dr Kazunori Baba and colleagues at the University of Tokyo's medical school said they had come up with improved equipped.

They added an extra three-dimensional probe to an existing 3-D scanner and tried it out on 66 normal foetuses. It produced an image every eight seconds, which could be viewed as a sort of slow-motion video.
It did not work well after 24 weeks because the baby was too big and did not record quick movements.
But "slow, yawn-like openings of the mouth and opening and shutting the hands appeared quite clearly in the sequence of images," they wrote.
They said it was a big improvement on conventional 3-D scans, which could only produce a still picture of the foetus.
